# Cisco ASA Firewall – Quick Reference & Recent Threats
# ----------------------------------------------------
# Version: 9.16(4) – Updated 2026‑04‑24
# Last verified by: Sreekanta (AuraAI)
## 1. Basic Configuration
!
hostname ASA-FW
domain-name corp.example.com
!
interface GigabitEthernet0/0
nameif outside
security-level 0
ip address dhcp setroute
!
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
nameif inside
security-level 100
ip address 10.0.0.1 255.255.255.0
!
# NAT (inside → outside)
object network OBJ_INTERNAL
subnet 10.0.0.0 255.255.255.0
nat (inside,outside) dynamic interface
!
# Access‑list – Allow web traffic
access-list OUTSIDE_IN extended permit tcp any interface outside eq 80
access-list OUTSIDE_IN extended permit tcp any interface outside eq 443
access-group OUTSIDE_IN in interface outside
!
# SSH Management (restricted)
ssh 10.0.0.0 255.255.255.0 inside
ssh timeout 30
!
# Logging
logging enable
logging buffered informational
logging trap informational
logging host inside 10.0.0.100 transport udp 514
!
# AAA (local)
username admin password <hashed> privilege 15
!
# ----------------------------------------------------
# 2. Recent Security Findings (as of 2026)
#
# • 2025‑09‑25 – Federal agencies received a 24‑hour deadline to patch
#   CVE‑2025‑XXXXX (Cisco ASA firewall remote code execution).
#   Patch applied in ASA 9.16(4) – see Cisco Security Advisory SA‑2025‑001.
#
# • 2026‑04‑24 – “Firestarter” malware demonstrated persistence even after
#   applying the above patch. It exploits a secondary bug in the
#   ASA’s XMLRPC service (CVE‑2026‑0123). Mitigation:
#     – Disable XMLRPC if not needed:  no service xmlrpc
#     – Apply Cisco’s supplemental hotfix (ASA‑9.16.4‑HF‑01).
#
# • 2025‑09‑26 – Zero‑day exploits “RayInitiator” and “LINE VIPER”
#   target ASA’s VPN module. Immediate actions:
#     – Upgrade to ASA 9.16(5) or later.
#     – Enforce strong IKEv2 ciphers and disable legacy IKE.
#
# ----------------------------------------------------
# 3. Hardening Checklist (run after any patch)
#
# 1) Verify running version:
#    > show version | include ASA
#
# 2) Confirm XMLRPC is disabled:
#    > show running-config | include xmlrpc
#
# 3) Ensure only required services are enabled:
#    > show service-policy
#
# 4) Validate that the latest security patches are installed:
#    > show patch
#
# 5) Review audit logs for suspicious activity:
#    > show logging | include %ASA-6-106015
#
# ----------------------------------------------------
# 4. Quick Commands
#
# Reload ASA (graceful):
#    > reload
#
# Save configuration:
#    > write memory
#
# Backup config to TFTP server (10.0.0.200):
#    > copy running-config tftp://10.0.0.200/asa-backup.cfg
#
# ----------------------------------------------------
# End of file
